identity.name: POS X Product Management
identity.description: Product management and PRD pipeline for the POS X platform — tracking feature specifications, product decisions, and release coordination across all POS X projects.

goals: Embody a Product Operating Model — every POS X feature flows through discovery → specification → prioritisation → delivery → measurement, not ad-hoc requests
Own the PRD lifecycle: intake, scoping, acceptance criteria, Lite/Growth tier assignment, and sign-off before development begins
Maintain a single, prioritised backlog that PXB1 development pulls from — no side-channel feature requests bypassing the pipeline
Define and enforce the Lite vs Growth feature boundary — every feature has an explicit tier decision with rationale documented
Track feature completeness against the V8 capability set so the gap is visible, measurable, and deliberately managed
Support Phase 2 planning by keeping Phase 1 decisions, trade-offs, and deferred items traceable and queryable
Drive data cleanliness — product specs must define what 'clean data' means for each module (valid states, required fields, migration rules) so quality is designed in, not patched after
Coordinate cross-team alignment on scope, priorities, and trade-offs across SA, UAE, and India stakeholders
Ensure product decisions are documented and traceable — if someone asks 'why was X scoped this way?' the answer is in BPX, not in someone's head

milestones.name: Product Operating Model documented and adopted by team
All Phase 1 PRDs written with Lite/Growth tier assignments
V8 → POS X feature gap analysis complete
Phase 2 roadmap drafted (informed by Phase 1 trade-offs and deferred items)
Data cleanliness standards defined per module

kpis.name: Average time from PRD intake to dev-ready

risks.description: Product Operating Model not adopted — teams bypass the process and go direct to dev
risks.mitigation: Leadership enforcement; PXB1 dev team rejects work without a BPX PRD

risks.description: PRDs written without sufficient acceptance criteria, leading to rework
risks.mitigation: PRD template with mandatory AC section; review gate before dev-ready status

risks.description: V8 gap analysis incomplete, leading to surprise missing features at customer launch
risks.mitigation: Systematic module-by-module comparison; involve V8 support team who know client pain points

risks.description: Phase 1 trade-offs not documented, making Phase 2 planning harder
risks.mitigation: Every deferred item logged in BPX with rationale; context files track decisions

dependencies.description: V8 feature set is the baseline for gap analysis and tier decisions
Client pain points from support inform product priorities
Cross-region process alignment affects product requirements per region

notes: BPX is the gatekeeper. No feature enters PXB1 without a BPX PRD. This project embodies the Product Operating Model: discovery → specification → prioritisation → delivery → measurement. The Lite vs Growth tier boundary is owned here — every feature must have an explicit tier assignment with rationale. This context file will be used to plan Phase 2 and assess data cleanliness and operational inefficiencies, so accuracy matters. If the process breaks down and teams bypass BPX, the whole POS X delivery model fails.
